instruction.text: Three friends spend an afternoon counting the different coloured cars that drive past their houses. Drag the tally marks to complete Jack and Brooke’s columns.
Fill in the remaining gaps in the tally chart.
Meteorologists recorded the hours of sunlight in July 2017 in different cities. Use the bar chart to complete the sentences.

atoms.b: The sun shone for the most amount of time in ((Athens Berlin ++Cape_Town Copenhagen Milan Nice Rome)).
The sun shone for the least amount of time in ((Athens Berlin Cape_Town ++Copenhagen Milan Nice Rome)).
There were ((100 150 ++200 250)) hours of sunlight in Milan.
In ((Athens Berlin Cape_Town Copenhagen Milan ++Nice ++Rome)) and ((Athens Berlin Cape_Town Copenhagen Milan ++Nice ++Rome)), there were the same number of hours of sunlight.

instruction.text: Looking at the bar chart, decide whether the statement is true, false or not shown.

atoms.a: In Berlin, the sun shone for exactly 100 hours.
The sun shone more in Athens than in Milan.
The weather in Nice and Rome was similarly rainy.

feedback.wrong: The bar chart only shows hours of sunlight. There is no information about rainfall.

atoms.a: Only Rome had 250 hours of sunlight.

feedback.wrong: Nice also had 250 hours of sunlight.

atoms.a: In Cape Town, the sun shone for over 250 hours.
In both Copenhagen and Stockholm, the sun shone for 100 hours.

feedback.wrong: The bar chart only shows the hours of sunlight for Copenhagen. Stockholm is not one of the recorded cities.
